redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_guard_secrets_read.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 2 of 707 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - bw1 (house FAIL), bw2 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 705/707 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; no .npmrc to carry or drop

outcome.technical: Added _config.task_covered_files and task_covered_outputs (task_binding first; broken binding covers nothing; bound tree reads the phase tree's plan restricted to the bound task; ordinary tree falls through to in_progress_task_map / in_progress_outputs). guard-secrets-read._ungoverned_write_target now calls task_covered_files instead of in_progress_files (nothing else about reading the command changed). require-plan steps 2c, 3 and 3b call the same two functions with the binding it already read, so the Edit and Bash arms share one reader. Tests: new stage _bound_worktree_cases in test_guard_secrets_read.py builds a real bound worktree whose shard copy has the bound task pending and a stale sibling in_progress (bw1 parity for declared / undeclared / stale-sibling-only file, plus explicit expected verdicts; bw2 two heredoc writes by a fresh session to two declared files allowed and no free file spent); tb11-tb14 in test__config.py cover the reader directly. test_guard_secrets_read 707/707, test__config 351/351, test_require_plan 236/236, test_guard_bash_writes 237/237, test__refs 286/286, bench-hooks --gate exit 0, ruff clean, vermin clean. NOT run: the full sweep (orchestrator). Note: a Bash heredoc write to _config.py was refused by the plan gate (change magnitude 82 > 80, 'outside the running task files'), which is the very symptom this task fixes seen on my own edit; I stopped using Bash for writes and made all edits with the Edit tool, which the gate allowed. guard-bash-writes.py:2045 (the post-hoc Stop/Post reporter) still calls in_progress_files on the worktree's own copy - outside this task's files and not the Bash-write PreToolUse path; left alone, a candidate follow-up.
outcome.descriptive: A task worktree's shell write and its Edit now read the same coverage, so declared files are allowed on the first and second heredoc write and a stale sibling's file is refused on both.

testsAdded: bw1 in a bound task worktree whose shard copy still reads the task pending, a Bash heredoc write and an Edit of the same declared file get the same verdict, and so do an undeclared file and a file only a stale sibling declares (carries tests.add entry of test_guard_secrets_read.py)
bw2 a second heredoc write to a declared file in a bound worktree is allowed, the first having spent no free file
tb11 a bound tree's coverage is the bound task's files out of the PHASE tree's plan
tb12 a tree whose binding cannot be proved covers nothing
tb13 an ordinary tree's coverage is its running tasks' files
